title: Landing page: seven elements that make it convert
metaTitle: Landing page: 7 elements that make it convert | Viesigners
description: A clear offer, a single action, proof, speed: the seven elements a landing page needs to turn visitors into inquiries.
summary: A high-performing landing page defends **one offer, for one audience, with one action.**
Clarity, proof and speed matter more than the amount of information.
Measuring from day one lets you improve the page with data.

body.p: A landing page is a page designed for a single action: request a quote, book a call, sign up. Everything that doesn't serve that action is friction.

ul: **A clear promise on the first screen:** who you help and what result you bring.
**A single main action:** one button, one verb, one promise. Secondary actions stay discreet.
**Value before features:** talk about what the person gets, not what you do.
**Credible proof:** quantified results, client logos, specific testimonials.
**Answers to objections:** price, timing, risk, comparison with alternatives.
**A form without needless friction:** only the necessary fields.
**A fast page on mobile:** one second too many costs inquiries.

body.p: Set up conversion tracking before you publish. Watch where visitors leave, test one change at a time (headline, button, proof) and keep what works.

We design [landing pages and sales funnels](@landing-pages) that have generated up to a 3,500% increase in inquiries with minimal ad budgets. If you want to make them even more profitable with [digital advertising](@publicite), that's possible too.

faq.q: How many fields should a landing page form have?
a: As few as possible: every extra field lowers the chance of a response. Ask only for what you need to take the next step.

faq.q: Should a landing page have a navigation menu?
a: Generally no. Removing navigation focuses the visitor on the main action and reduces leaks.
